claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be prepared in an initially single-phase high-temperature BCC state.
The initial high-temperature BCC phase is disordered.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the alloy's BCC phase at high temperature.
Al-induced local ordering provides a thermodynamic driving force that competes with configurational-entropy stabilization.
Al–Ni interactions in this alloy have a negative mixing enthalpy.
At intermediate temperatures, the enthalpic driving force for Al–Ni ordering can overcome configurational-entropy stabilization.
The proposed ordering transformation occurs only when diffusion kinetics are sufficiently active.
Isothermal holding between approximately 700 and 1000 °C will produce local partitioning of Al.
Ni will partition in association with Al during intermediate-temperature holding.
Al and Ni partitioning will generate B2-type ordered domains within the BCC matrix.
Formation of the ordered phase will occur at the expense of the disordered BCC matrix.
Within the stated temperature range, samples held at lower temperatures will develop increasing ordered-phase fractions relative to the initial BCC state.
The emergence of the ordered phase will be detectable by X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy.
Intermediate-temperature holding will increase hardness relative to the initial BCC baseline.
A reduced-Al composition would be less prone to ordering under the same thermal conditions.
Oxidation or extreme cooling rates can inhibit the proposed diffusion-controlled ordering.
